correctness.rationale: Direct Brownian covariance integration gives an exact cubic gain and positive scalar variance. The derivative numerator has derivative 2(1-h-2t) times a positive denominator, hence increases then decreases once. Its positive left endpoint and exact right endpoint sign establish unique global solution in all parameter ranges, including equality. F has one root inside (0,1); implicit differentiation proves monotonicity and algebraic limits. Exact SymPy identities and 75 independent numerical quadratures plus grid optimization reproduced the package checks; finite sampling was not used to establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Continuous monitoring instruments often average over a nonzero exposure window. The exact two-parameter optimum shows when a terminal exposure is better than an interior one, pinpoints an algebraic width frontier and a noise frontier, and proves a singular point-width limit. These are natural and actionable classification facts beyond routine substitution into the standard covariance update; the theorem intentionally excludes width-dependent noise models and multiple sensors.
